quest.title: The Lone Isle Glimpsed Through Fog
quest.description: The lonely isle appeared in silence through the dark fog of night. Wherever shall it lead you...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x20, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

chapter.title: The Lone Isle Glimpsed Through Fog

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Good work, everyone! We're looking to wrap with our two main ladies today. I can already smell our success, hehe!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you mean, "looking to wrap"?

choices.text: It means completing the filming of all of their scenes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh! Aren't you the expert now!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: This upcoming scene is the Two Musketeers' final confrontation with the baron. There'll be quite a bit of action, but no choreography beyond what we've already rehearsed.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Anyway, get ready! Lights, Kamera, ACTION!

response.speaker: "Baron"
response.text: The view is beautiful tonight... It reminds me of that fateful night ten years ago.

response.speaker: "Baron"
response.text: Hmm, and now that I've said it, I can even make out the faint fragrance of herbal tea in the air.

response.speaker: "Iris"
response.text: Enough, villain. It's time that you pay for the death of our mother.

response.speaker: "Baron"
response.text: My dear Iris, have you forgotten your manners? How can you speak like this to your own father?

response.speaker: "Tulipe"
response.text: I'd sooner swallow all of my teeth than call you "father."

response.speaker: "Baron"
response.text: What did I expect... seems the daughters have turned out to be just as obstinate as their foolish mother.

response.speaker: "Baron"
response.text: In this world, Mora and status is everything.

response.speaker: "Baron"
response.text: She thought she could blackmail me using her children and force me to grant her recognition and concessions? Ah, how naive can a woman be?

response.speaker: "Iris"
response.text: Mother never asked a single thing of you. All she wished was for us to live a peaceful life, just like the others.

response.speaker: "Tulipe"
response.text: It was you who personally brewed the poison of prejudice and sent mother to her death.

response.speaker: "Tulipe"
response.text: Compared to that deadly poison, the two bullets that will soon pierce through your heart will be like sweet mercy.

response.speaker: "Baron"
response.text: Hahaha, and that's exactly why I said you're just as naive as her. Did you really think two muskets would be enough to defeat me?

response.speaker: "Baron"
response.text: So, let's see. What is stronger — Mora and power, or the two muskets in your hands?

choices.text: It means finalizing everything we've recorded for them so far.

talks.objective: Film a scene of revenge and defeat opponents

dialogues.speaker: "Tulipe"
dialogues.text: You've lost.

dialogues.speaker: "Baron"
dialogues.text: Tch... To think I'd lose to my own two kids...

dialogues.speaker: "Iris"
dialogues.text: We are no children of yours, and we'll never call that place our home.

dialogues.speaker: "Baron"
dialogues.text: Hmph... Then tell me, what did you do all of this for?

dialogues.speaker: "Baron"
dialogues.text: You lost your mother, and will soon kill your father as well. What will you gain in the end other than sentences for your crimes?

dialogues.speaker: "Tulipe"
dialogues.text: We will gain... our long-awaited justice.

dialogues.speaker: "Tulipe"
dialogues.text: (Gunshot)

dialogues.speaker: "Tulipe"
dialogues.text: ...It's over.

dialogues.speaker: "Iris"
dialogues.text: ...Finally, it's over.

dialogues.speaker: "Iris"
dialogues.text: So. Where will you go now, Tulipe?

dialogues.speaker: "Tulipe"
dialogues.text: I'm not too sure, Iris. Maybe somewhere with lots of flowers... After all, mother always did love going where the blossoms were. What about you?

dialogues.speaker: "Iris"
dialogues.text: I want to go visit mother's grave.

dialogues.speaker: "Tulipe"
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's not a bad idea...

dialogues.speaker: "Iris"
dialogues.text: Huh!? Tulipe, look!

dialogues.speaker: "Tulipe"
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: "Iris"
dialogues.text: It's mother's favorite, the Rainbow Rose. Look... it's blooming again.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: *claps*

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Excellent, that was beyond mesmerizing! Even I didn't expect this scene to go so well. And we got it in a single take!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Alright everyone, we've got a wrap for Tulipe and Iris!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Congratulations, Ayaka and Chevreuse!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Thank you. I didn't expect our parts to wrap so quickly... I wish I could savor the experience for just a bit longer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon totally understands! Paimon's not ready to say goodbye to the clapperboard, either. Filming has really been a lot of fun!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You were great too, Chevreuse! The way you said "long-awaited justice"... It gave Paimon chills!

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: That is indeed my favorite line in the whole book. I still remember trying to act it out in my room the first few times I read it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, Paimon would've never guessed you're that type...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Who doesn't like stories where the guilty are punished, and justice prevails over evil? Don't forget, I'm the Captain of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol.

response.speaker: Letellier
response.text: Captain! I have something urgent to report.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: ...Please excuse me, everyone. I'll be back in just a moment.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's okay, don't worry about us!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Oh, was she whisked away by work already? I was just about to tell her how great she did.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: It seemed like some urgent official business.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Ah, then perhaps we should thank the stars that we were able to wrap both of your parts so quickly today. Switching around the filming schedule would have been a real pain.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Anyway, I actually came over to let everyone know that we're all done for today. You can go home and get some rest!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: And one last thing, Miss Ayaka. Your acting skills today were immaculate as always. Are you sure you won't consider taking up full-time acting? See, I just happen to know this great troupe that's still looking for a lead actress...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Thank you for your kind words, Director Furina. Unfortunately... there are still many matters that I have to take care of back home at the Yashiro Commission. I cannot remain in Fontaine to pursue an acting career.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Nevertheless, I will make sure to treasure this incredible opportunity in my heart.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: That's a shame, but I understand. Just let me know if you ever change your mind.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: I believe it's also about time for me to take my leave. But hopefully I'll see you on set over the next few days — even though my part's wrapped, I'd still like to swing by and help out the crew.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: #See you tomorrow, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep! See you tomorrow!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, what should we do next? Maybe we'll go investigate the case some more with Chevreuse today?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, please come with me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Wh—Where are we going?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: You could say... that our ship has finally chanced upon one of those "small, remote islands of intel."

choices.text: Great job, you've already wrapped your roles!

talks.objective: Go with Chevreuse to investigate the clues

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... Paimon's exhausted. Paimon definitely didn't expect having to float this far after a full day of filming...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, Chevreuse, why did you take us here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you find a new clue?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Affirmative. It wasn't anything conclusive, but it should show us a clear way forward.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Have you ever heard of someone by the name of Emilie?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean that famous perfumer?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: She's a good friend of mine. She's lent me her aid several times in the past to resolve some difficult cases.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: After I discovered the Rainbow Rose at the scene of the murder, I sent it to her. After all, she's probably the foremost expert on flowers and scents in all of Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And then...?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: There was nothing remarkable about the flower, or the trace amounts of soil left on it.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: But according to Emilie, the Rainbow Rose left by the killer was derived from a very rare cultivar.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, Paimon didn't know that there were different varieties of Rainbow Rose! Paimon just thought that they grew everywhere in the wild...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Flowers that are deliberately cultivated will always show some different features from those that bloom in the wild.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: We already knew that the rose left at the scene belonged to a special cultivar, but with Emilie's expertise, we were able to pinpoint the place where it was first picked from.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohh! Paimon gets it now. So whoever first planted that Rainbow Rose was probably the killer!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Precisely. And after we checked what we learned against some sales records from the past, we discovered that there's only one person in all of Fontaine who could grow and sell this specific cultivar.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, really? And who is it?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: It's the novelist.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But didn't you say that he had an alibi?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: To be clear, I haven't changed my mind about him. I still don't think he was the one who pulled the trigger.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: However, that doesn't mean that the true culprit never visited him at his home, or never purchased a Rainbow Rose from his garden.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Whatever the case, we will have to confirm a number of things with him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you mean, the next place we need to go is...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Yes, we're going to pay him a visit at his home.

talks.objective: Go to the place Chevreuse mentioned

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: That should be his house.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There are so many Gardemeks stationed around the place... Uh, that's pretty unusual, right?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: According to what he told me the last time we spoke, he hired them so he won't be harassed or disturbed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so there are a lot of flowers in his garden... But Paimon doesn't think we'll be able to pick one without alerting the Gardemeks.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Right, which is exactly why I think there has to be a special connection between him and the killer.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So should we... knock?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Just wait here for now. I'd like to take care of a number of those Gardemeks first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But they're so far away... How are you planning to do that?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Don't forget, Paimon, I'm actually the real life captain of the musketeers.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: All clear. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait wait wait... Paimon's a little nervous now that we know he could be the killer. Can we go over our plan of action again?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I'll go knock on the door, and make sure it's safe inside. Once we're sure that we're in the clear, I'll ask him to come with us for a quick round of questioning at the Gardes' headquarters.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But can't we just arrest him?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: We still have no evidence that he's the killer, or that he lent the killer any direct aid.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Still, it would be appreciated if you could pick a Rainbow Rose from his garden for me while I'm talking to him. It will help the Marechaussee Phantom confirm Emilie's theory.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure, no problem! Just be careful, Chevreuse.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Excuse me, Mr. Baptiste? Are you home?

dialogues.speaker: Baptiste
dialogues.text: Who could it be at this hour... Ah, it's you, Officer Chevreuse.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Would you mind accompanying me to the Gardes headquarters, Mr. Baptiste? We would like to ask you some questions about a case.

dialogues.speaker: Baptiste
dialogues.text: Oh, is it still regarding the murder case from before?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I cannot confirm or deny that at this time.

dialogues.speaker: Baptiste
dialogues.text: So it is, then.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Listen, I need you to come with me, Mr. Baptiste.

dialogues.speaker: Baptiste
dialogues.text: *sigh* Miss Chevreuse, I'll save you the trouble. Oh, and you two over there, there's no need for you to pick my flowers, either. It's not time for them to bloom yet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, uh okay...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: By "saving me the trouble," you mean...

dialogues.speaker: Baptiste
dialogues.text: I will confess. I was the killer.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He... He just admitted he's guilty!

dialogues.speaker: Baptiste
dialogues.text: Please relax, everyone. I am not armed. The musket you're looking for has been buried in my backyard.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: ...Then it's my responsibility to inform you, Mr. Baptiste, that everything you say right now will be used as evidence for the inevitable trial.

dialogues.speaker: Baptiste
dialogues.text: Yes. I am perfectly aware of that.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: ...I must say, I hate this feeling.

dialogues.speaker: Baptiste
dialogues.text: Oh? Is it because I confessed, or because you've been proven wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Both, I suppose.

choices.text: That guy in the Fleuve Cendre...

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: For the same reason as the one I wrote out in my novel, of course. I did it to exact revenge.

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: I know you haven't figured out the link between the two of us. Had you done so, I'd have been taken away to the headquarters a long time ago.

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: But that won't stop me from always remembering his grotesque face. After all, he was the one who killed my mother.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: ...Your mother is still healthy and well.

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: You know I was adopted as a child. I was referring to my birth mother.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: That was never recorded in the orphanage's records...

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: Please forgive a six-year-old child for concocting some lies to protect himself after watching his mother die right in front of him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... your novel... it was like a record of your life?

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: No, of course not. It was a work of fiction with many embellished parts.

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: But... I am indeed the illegitimate son of a wealthy and influential man, who abused his power to murder my mother. That part was a hundred percent real.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: But the man you killed didn't have a Mora to his name.

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: He was a hired assassin, an irredeemable beast who sank his fangs into a defenseless woman just for a few bags of Mora.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: But if that's really the truth... You wouldn't be telling us any of this now. You still haven't managed to take revenge against your father, the true mastermind behind it all.

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: ...Haha, I never thought I'd hear that kind of thing from the Captain of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I'm simply skeptical about your motives.

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: It's simple, really. I've grown tired of everything, and don't want to shoulder this burden anymore.

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: You may have considered me too soft to pull the trigger. Well, as it turns out, you are exactly right. I've become overwhelmed by the aftermath of the murder.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: So you're going to call a stop to your revenge, just like that?

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: The true mastermind is too rich and too powerful for me. I've accepted that I will never be able to avenge my mother alone.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: And so what? The characters in your book never gave up.

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: Now, Officer Chevreuse, I'm the one who has killed a man, aren't I? Are you trying to convince me to commit another crime?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: What's your father's name? How do you plan to prove the veracity of all of your claims?

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: Well, ahem... I'd like to speak with you privately.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Sure. Why don't we speak privately at the Gardes headquarters?

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: No, it has to be here. I must ensure that we won't be overheard.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: ...Fine. Let's talk here.

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: When I said "won't be overheard," I meant by anyone...

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: I would like to speak with you and you alone.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Thanks, I appreciate it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Please stay safe, Chevreuse!

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Alright. Let's hear it.

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: ...Will you really believe what I'm about to say?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Well, that depends on what you're going to tell me.

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: Heh... Fair enough, fair enough. Then listen closely...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Baptiste utters a name...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: So that's how it's connected.

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: So, it seems you believe me after all.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Do you want me to go public with this?

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: No, of course not. At least, not right now.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Then, why did you bother telling me?

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: You've read my work. What do you think?

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: Even if you were to go public with all of this right now, he'd simply deny everything.

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: It's been too long... almost twenty years. Anything that could be used as evidence has long faded away. Even if there might have been a solitary island of truth once upon a time, it has long sunk beneath the waves by now.

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: Justice will never find him.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Not if you don't try.

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: I know that as the Captain of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, you will always stand on the side of justice.

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: But... do you really think a cushy life in prison really constitutes "justice" for him? I bet he could lead an extremely comfortable life in the Fortress of Meropide.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: What are you trying to say?

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: I've been observing you from a distance. Your portrayal of the musketeer was exquisite.

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: Pull the trigger of justice against him. Let the villain get what he deserves.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: ...You want me to let you go, so you may complete your revenge?

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: No, Officer Chevreuse. I know that would be impossible.

response.speaker: Baptiste
response.text: No, what I'd like is for you to perform the deed on my behalf.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Meanwhile, not far away...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh... Chevreuse sure is taking her time! What could they be talking about, anyway?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's worried... What if he decided to attack her?

choices.text: I have full confidence in Chevreuse's fighting skills.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, uh... You do have a point.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, do you have any idea who the rich person might be? And why the novelist doesn't want us to hear what he's saying to Chevreuse?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Sorry to keep you waiting, you two.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! How did your talk go?

choices.text: Did you figure out who the rich person he mentioned was?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I've already sent someone to escort Baptiste back to the headquarters for questioning. He wasn't lying about the musket — it was indeed buried in his backyard.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But what about the name? Did he tell you the name of the rich guy?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Yes, he did. But for now, I have to return to the Special Patrol. There are still a few loose ends I need to tie up.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (What's going on? It feels like she's keeping something from us.)

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I'll probably be quite busy over the next few days, so apologies if you don't see me on set.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, Paimon understands if you can't tell us everything you know! We'll just keep an eye on The Steambird, then.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: ...Actually, there's still something else I need your help with.

choices.text: If anything, he's the one I'd be worried about.
We can go somewhere else for now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's filming time again! Our schedule is jam-packed for the next couple of days, too. We've got so many different locations and sets to cover...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's head out and meet up with the others!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Both the filming and the criminal investigation progress at a steady pace over the next few days...

dialogues.speaker: "Baron"
dialogues.text: Get them!

dialogues.speaker: "Iris"
dialogues.text: Tulipe! There are too many of them!

dialogues.speaker: "Tulipe"
dialogues.text: It'll be okay! We'll cover each other, Iris.

dialogues.speaker: "Tulipe"
dialogues.text: And mother will be watching over us, too.
